newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA STATE DECLARES SATURDAY HOLIDAY.
newsitem.headline: INDIA STATE DECLARES SATURDAY HOLIDAY.

text.p: India's western Maharashtra state said on Thursday it had declared August 9 a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act.
August 9 marks the 50th anniversary of the beginning of the "Quit India" movement, Indian nationalists' last great push in their campaign to win independence from the British.
"Being the second Saturday, it is anyway a government holiday, but the state government has declared a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act," a state government official told Reuters.
The "Quit India" campaign was launched from Bombay's August Kranti grounds on August 9, 1942. A series of commemorative events has been planned for Saturday to mark the golden jubilee.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral is scheduled to attend a grand concluding function at the August Kranti ground late on Saturday.
